beats.text: It did not come from an observatory.
beats.note: The planet was found at Lowell Observatory in Arizona. The name was suggested at a breakfast table in Oxford, England.

beats.text: The discovery was announced on 13 March 1930.
beats.note: The next morning, 14 March, Falconer Madan of the Bodleian Library read the story in The Times and mentioned it to his granddaughter.

beats.context: Venetia Burney's age when she suggested the name Pluto for the new planet.

beats.note: Madan passed her suggestion to Herbert Hall Turner, an astronomer and a friend of his.

beats.text: Turner cabled it to Lowell Observatory.
beats.note: As reported by Mental Floss and Today I Found Out, it read: 'Naming new planet, please consider PLUTO, suggested by small girl Venetia Burney for dark and gloomy planet.'

beats.name: Venetia Burney
beats.role: Her grandfather rewarded her with five pounds for the name.

beats.text: Eleven years old. Five pounds. A world named.
